# One requirement per line; format: <source-L-doc>: <description>

L10: Verify the per-stack data interface is exactly 1024 bits (16 channels x 64 bits).
L10: Verify each 64-bit channel operates as two independent 32-bit pseudo-channels.
L10: Verify the 16 channels are independent: a command on one channel does not affect another.
L10: Verify channels need not be synchronous (drive skewed/async clocks).
L10: Verify per-pin data rate up to 6.4 Gb/s/pin and up to 819 GB/s per stack.
L10: Verify commands are registered at the rising edges of CK_t/CK_c.
L10: Verify write data framed by WDQS and read data by RDQS at double data rate.
L10: Verify 8-Hi -> 16 GB and 12-Hi -> 24 GB from 16 Gb dies.
L10: Verify on-die ECC corrects a single-bit array error transparently.
L10: Verify link ECC detects/corrects a transmission error and reports uncorrectable cases.
L10: Verify refresh management (RFM) under sustained high activate rates.
L10: Verify command/address parity error reported via the RAS alert path.
L10: Verify soft-repair maps out a failing row/column.
L10: Verify temperature (TEMP) drives refresh-rate adaptation.
L10: Verify mode-register set/read per channel with the channel idle.
L10: Verify bank-group back-to-back column access timing.
L10: Verify TSV / microbump integrity via base-die IEEE-1500 / direct-access test.
L10: Verify power-down and self-refresh entry/exit per channel.
L16: 1024-bit-wide data interface per stack (16 channels x 64 bits).
L16: 16 completely independent channels; each with its own differential clock and command/address bus.
L16: Channels not necessarily synchronous to each other.
L16: Each 64-bit channel divisible into two independent 32-bit pseudo-channels.
L16: Up to 6.4 Gb/s per pin; up to 819 GB/s per stack.
L16: Commands registered at the rising edges of CK_t/CK_c.
L16: Write data framed by WDQS, read data by RDQS, double data rate.
L16: 8-Hi (16 GB) / 12-Hi (24 GB) stacks of 16 Gb dies on TSV + microbumps on a 2.5D silicon interposer.
L16: On-die ECC and link ECC.
L16: Refresh Management (RFM) to bound disturbance.
L16: RAS: command/address parity, soft-repair, error/alert reporting.
L16: Bank-group architecture for back-to-back column access.
